name: BSP_Session_DrainMessageQueue

name: BSP_Session_EnqueueIncomingMessage
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet cc_unit_orders_apply, read-only analysis. void __thiscall(session, peer), RET 4, body 0076E520..0076E70C. Reads the packet through peer vtable[1] into a 400h-byte stack buffer, builds the message with the factory 00768530, sets msg+18h from peer+174h and msg+14h from peer+14h, then appends to the vector at session+24Ch. Ghidra drops the reachable tail after _free (CALL_RETURN override); the listing is complete. docs/UNIT_STATE_MESSAGE.md | Packet cc2_session_dispatch: __thiscall(session = ECX, message, sender), not (session, peer). The local path is a serialise and rebuild round trip, not a pointer hand-off: 0076E561 sets up a 400h-byte stack stream, 0076E575 calls message->vtable[4](stream) and 0076E5A4 calls 00768530(stream) to build a second message from those bytes. The copy is then stamped: 0076E5B2 copy+18h = sender+174h, 0076E5C6 00782790(copy, [00F876B0]) the current tick, 0076E5CB copy+14h = the source MESSAGE's +14h (MOV EDX,[EDI+0x14] with EDI = [ESP+448h], the message), correcting docs/UNIT_STATE_MESSAGE.md's peer+14h. Append: 0076E5D1 takes the interlocked path through [00CE221C] when session+258h is null, the reallocating path at 0076E5F5 otherwise. Because the copy carries the current tick, the drain applies it in the same fixed step. See docs/SESSION_MESSAGE_DISPATCH.md.
